title: Coprime
statementMd:
"Why did it come to this? I finally met someone I love, and also gained a lifelong best friend. Two kinds of joy blend together, and this double joy brings endless more happiness. I was supposed to embrace a dreamlike happy life. But why... why has everything turned out like this?"

Given a positive integer $n$, consider all positive integers in the interval $[n, n^2]$.

A positive integer $k$ is defined as **good** if it meets both of the following requirements:

- $n \le k \le n^2$.
- For any positive integer $i$ in $[n, n^2]$ where $i \neq k$, we have $\gcd(i, k) = 1$.

For the given $n$, you are required to:

- Count how many good positive integers exist in $[n, n^2]$;
- Output any one of these good positive integers.

## Input

The first line contains a positive integer $T$ $(1 \le T \le 5000)$, indicating the number of test cases. Each of the next $T$ lines contains a positive integer $n$ $(1 \le n \le 5000)$.

## Output

For each test case, output two lines. The first line contains a non-negative integer $c$, representing the number of good integers in $[n, n^2]$. The second line contains a positive integer $k \in [n, n^2]$ which is a good integer. If there are multiple answers, you may output any of them.

As a special case: if no good integer exists in $[n, n^2]$, output $0$ on the first line and $-1$ on the second line.
